title: Noise data step by step and learn to undo it
brief: Build linear and cosine schedules, the closed-form forward process, conversions between noise, data, velocity, and score, the DDPM posterior, the training loss, and ancestral sampling, then train a DDPM on 2-D data.
hints: Keep index 0 for the data: torch.cat([torch.zeros(1), torch.linspace(beta_1, beta_T, T)]) gives betas[t] for t = 1..T, and torch.cumprod(1 - betas, 0) then starts at 1.
In q_sample, alpha_bar[t].reshape(-1, *[1] * (x0.dim() - 1)) broadcasts one step per example over every other axis.
The posterior variance at t uses alpha_bar[t - 1]; with the index-0 convention that is 1 at t = 1, so the variance there is 0.
In ddpm_sample, add no noise on the last step, t = 1.
